verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              कुन्तीपुत्रस्तु तं मन्त्रं स्मरन्नेव धनञ्जयः।  प्रतिज्ञामात्मनो रक्षन्मुमोहाचिन्त्यविक्रमः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Then Dhananjaya the son of Kunti, possessed of inconceivable prowess thinking of how to redeem his vow, recollected the mantras (obtained from Vyasa); and soon was he lost of sleep.

verses.sanskrit: तं तु शोकेन संतप्तं स्वप्ने कपिवरध्वजम्। आससाद महातेजा ध्यायन्तं गरुडध्वजः ॥२॥
verses.english: Then the highly puissant god having the Garuda as an emblem on his banner, appeared before the ape-bannered Arjuna merged in thought and burning with grief, in his dream.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युत्थानं च कृष्णस्य सर्वावस्थो धनञ्जयः। न लोपयति धर्मात्मा भक्त्या प्रेम्णा च सर्वदा ॥३॥
verses.english: The pious-souled Dhananjaya through the love and venevation he bore for Krishna, never failed under any circumstance, to rise up and advance a few steps for welcoming him.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युत्थाय च गोविन्दं स तस्मा आसनं ददौ। न चासने स्वयं बुद्धिं बीभत्सुर्व्यद‌धात् तदा ॥४॥
verses.english: Standing up therefore (in his dream), he welcomed Govinda and offered him a seat, He himself however then did not think of resuming his own seat.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृष्णो महातेजा जानन् पार्थस्य निश्चयम्। कुन्तीपुत्रमिदं वाक्यमासीनः स्थितमब्रवीत् ॥५॥
verses.english: Thus seated, Krishna of mighty energy, knowing what resolution Partha had formed, said these words to the son of Kunti, while the latter was standing before him.

verses.sanskrit: मा विषादे मनः पार्थ कृथाः कालो हि दुर्जयः।  कालः सर्वाणि भूतानि नियच्छति परे विधौ ॥६॥
verses.english: O Son of Pritha, let not your heart give way to sorrow. Time is invincible. It is time that compels all creatures to take to the inevitable course.

verses.sanskrit: किमर्थं च विषादस्ते तद्ब्रूहि द्विपदां वर। न शोच्यं विदुषां श्रेष्ठ शोकः कार्यविनाशनः ॥७॥
यत्तु कार्यं भवेत् कार्यं कर्मणा तत् समाचर।  हीनचेष्टस्य यः शोकः स हि शत्रुर्धनञ्जय ॥८॥
शोचन्नन्दयते शत्रून् कर्शयत्यपि बान्धवान्। क्षीयते च नरस्तस्मान्न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥९॥
verses.english: A man giving way to grief delights his enemies and saddens his friends and himself becomes reduced in (strength). Therefore you should not grieve.
verses.bhavadeepa: कार्यं कृत्यं कार्यं करणीयं भवेत् इत्यन्वयः ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन बीभत्सुरपराजितः।  आबभाषे तदा विद्वानिदं वचनमर्थवत् ॥१०॥
verses.english: Having been thus spoken to by the son of Vasudeva, the invincible and learned Vibhatsu said these words of (grave) signification to the former

verses.sanskrit: मया प्रतिज्ञा महती जयद्रथवधे कृता। श्वोऽस्मि हन्ता दुरात्मानं पुत्रघ्नमिति केशव ॥११॥
verses.english: I have taken a terrible oath in vowing to slaughter Jayadratha. Tomorrow shall I slay, O Keshava that wicked-souled slayer of my son.

verses.sanskrit: मत्प्रतिज्ञाविघातार्थं धार्तराष्ट्रैः किलाच्युत।  पृष्ठतः सैन्धवः कार्यः सर्वैर्गुप्तो महारथैः ॥१२॥
दश चैका च ताः कृष्ण अक्षौहिण्यः सुदुर्जयाः। हतावशेषास्तत्रेमा हन्त माधव संख्यया ॥१३॥
verses.english: Alas! O Mahadeva, their invincible army of one and ten Akshauhini strong, consists of the remnants of their soldiers (slain during the last compaign).

verses.sanskrit: ताभिः परिवृतः संख्ये सर्वैश्चैव महारथैः।  कथं शक्येत संद्रष्टुं दुरात्मा कृष्ण सैन्धवः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Surrounded by all these troops, as also by all their mighty car-warriors, how could that wicked-souled ruler of the Sindhus, O Krishna, be seen (by us)?

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञापारणं चापि न भविष्यति केशव। प्रतिज्ञायां च हीनायां कथं जीवति मद्विधः ॥१५॥
दुःखोपायस्य मे वीर विकांक्षा परिवर्तते।  द्रुतं च याति सविता तत एतद्ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: O hero, despondency stares me at the face, me whose only consolation now is in grief. I also tell you this that (during this period of the year) the sun runs his heavenly course swiftly.

verses.sanskrit: शोकस्थानं तु तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थस्य द्विजकेतनः।  संस्पृश्यांभस्ततः कृष्णः प्राङ्मुखः समवस्थितः ॥१७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: दुःखोपायस्य दुःखद्वारस्य प्रतिज्ञायाः विकांक्षा विसंवादः परिवर्तते प्रतिभाति ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: इदं वाक्यं महातेजा बभाषे पुष्करेक्षणः।  हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्धवस्य वधे कृती ॥१८॥
verses.english: Thereafter that highly puissant one of eyes like lotus-petals, said these words, for the welfare of Pandu's son who had resolved upon the slaughter of the Sindhu king.

verses.sanskrit: पार्थ पाशुपतं नाम परमास्त्रं सनातनम्।  येन सर्वान् मृधे दैत्यान् जघ्ने देवो महेश्वरः ॥१९॥
verses.english: "O Son of Pritha, there is a weapon excellent and eternal known by the name of Pasupata. By means of this weapon the god Mahesvare (in days gone by) slew all the Daityas in battle.

verses.sanskrit: यदि तद्विदितं तेऽद्य श्वो हन्ताऽसि जयद्रथ।  अथाज्ञातं प्रपद्यस्व मनसा वृषभध्वजम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: If today it be with your recollection, then tomorrow you will be able to slay Jayadratha. If it is unknown to you now, then do you worship in you mind the god having the bull for his emblein.

verses.sanskrit: तं देवं मनसा ध्यात्वा जोषमास्व धनञ्जय।  ततस्तस्य प्रसादात्त्वं भक्तः प्राप्स्यसि तन्महत् ॥२१॥
verses.english: Meditating on that god in your mind. do you hold communion with him. You are his devotee and in this way, through his grace only, can you expect to obtain that valuable treasure (Pasupata weapon).”

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृष्णवचः श्रुत्वा संस्पृश्यांभो धनञ्जयः।  भूमावासीन एकाग्रो जगाम मनसा भवम् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Thereupon, having heard Krishna's words and having rinsed his mouth with water, Dhananjaya sat down on the ground; and with a singleness of heart, began to adore Siva (in his mind).

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रणिहितो ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते शुभलक्षणे।  आत्मानमर्जुनोऽपश्यद्गगने सह‌केशवम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Thus rapt up in meditation, Arjuna saw himself and Keshava roving in the skies, just when the hour Brahma of auspicious indication set in.

verses.sanskrit: पुण्यं हिमवतः पादं मणिमन्तं च पर्वतम्।  ज्योतिर्भिश्च समाकीर्णं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Then it seemed that Parth held by his right arın by the lord Keshava and endued with the fleetness of the wind, reached the root of the sacred Himavat mountain teeming with gems, abounding in luminous objects and inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas. He was then accompanied by Keshava.

verses.sanskrit: वायुवेगगतिः पार्थः स्वं भेजे सहकेशवः।  केशवेन गृहीतः स दक्षिणे विभुना भुजे ॥२५॥
प्रेक्षमाणो बहून् भावान् जगामाद्भुतदर्शनान्।  उदीच्यां दिशि धर्मात्मा सोऽपश्यच्छ्वेतपर्वतम् ॥२६॥
verses.english: It seemed that he saw, as he went, many wonderful sight and objects; that one of righteous soul then saw on the Northern direction the white mountain.

verses.sanskrit: कुबेरस्य विहारे च नलिनीं पद्मभूषिताम्।  सरिच्छ्रेष्ठां च तां गङ्गां वीक्षमाणो बहूदकाम् ॥२७॥
सदा पुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैरुपेतां स्फटिकोपलाम्।  सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकीर्णां नानामृगसमाकुलाम् ॥२८॥
पुण्याश्रमवतीं रम्यां मनोज्ञांडजसेविताम्।  मन्दरस्य प्रदेशांश्च किन्नरोद्गीतनादितान् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Then he saw the regions about the Mandara mountains, regions that abounded in trees bearing blossoms and fruits; that were covered with pebbles and transparent crystals, that were infested with lions and tigers; that abounded in many other animals, that contained many sacred hermitages; that were charming; that there frequented by beautiful birds and that ever rang with the melodious songs of the Kinnaras.

verses.sanskrit: हेमरूप्यमयैः शृङ्गेर्नानौषधिविदीपितान्। तथा मन्दारवृक्षैश्च पुष्पितैरुपशोभितान् ॥३०॥
verses.english: The mountain itself was graced with gold and silver peaks blazing with various herbs and Oshadhis; and it was beautiful with numerous Mandara trees decked with blossoms.

verses.sanskrit: स्निग्धांजनचयाकारं संप्राप्तः कालपर्वतम्।  ब्रह्मतुङ्गनदीश्चान्यास्तथा जनपदानपि ॥३१॥
verses.english: He then arrived at the black mountains that looked like a heap of collyrium and after that, at the Brahmatunga, at many rivers and at many countries.

verses.sanskrit: स तुङ्गं शतशृङ्गं च शर्यातिवनमेव च। पुण्यमश्वशिरःस्थानं स्थानमाथर्वणस्य च ॥३२॥
verses.english: He then reached the Sutunga and the Shatashringa hills and the woods known by the name of Sharyati. Then he went to the holy place called Ashvashiras and also to the one known by the name of Artharvana.

verses.sanskrit: वृषदंशं च शैलेन्द्रं महामन्दरमेव च।  अप्सरोभिः समाकीर्णं किन्नरैश्चोपशोभितम् ॥३३॥
तस्मिन् शैले व्रजन् पार्थः सकृष्णः समवैक्षत। शुभैः प्रस्त्रवणैर्जुष्टां हेमधातुविभूषिताम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: Then roaming on that hill in the company of Krishna, Pritha's son beheld a plot of earth abounding in soothing springs, teeming with gold and other minerals, burning with the effulgence of the sun or moon and possessing a large number towns and cities. He also beheld various seas and numerous rich mines of wealth.

verses.sanskrit: चन्द्ररश्मिप्रकाशाङ्गीं पृथिवीं पुरमालिनीम्। समुद्रांश्चाद्भुताकारानपश्यद्बहुलाकरान् ॥३५॥
वियद्द्यां पृथिवीं चैव तथा विष्णुपदं व्रजन्।  विस्मितः सह कृष्णेन क्षिप्तो बाण इवाभ्यगात् ॥३६॥
ग्रहनक्षत्रसोमानां सूर्याग्न्योश्च समत्विषम्। अपश्यत तदा पार्थो ज्वलन्तमिव पर्वतम्  ॥३७॥
verses.english: Partha then beheld a mountain blazing as if with the effulgence of the planets, the stars, the moon, the sun and the fire.

verses.sanskrit: समासाद्य तु तं शैलं शैलाग्रे समवस्थितम्।  तपोनित्यं महात्मानमपश्यद्वृषभध्वजम् ॥३८॥
verses.english: He saw the god burning in his own energy like a thousand suns; holding the trident; with matted locks on his head; of milk-white complexion; and wearing barks and tiger skins.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रमिव सूर्याणां दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा।  शूलिनं जटिलं गौरं वल्कलाजिनवाससम् ॥३८॥
verses.english: He saw the god burning in his own energy like a thousand suns; holding the trident; with matted locks on his head; of milk-white complexion; and wearing barks and tiger skins.

verses.sanskrit: नयनानां सहस्रैश्च विचित्राङ्गं महौजसम्।  पार्वत्या सहितं देवं भूतसङ्घैश्च भास्वरैः ॥४०॥
गीतवादित्रसन्नादैर्हास्यलास्यसमन्वितम्।  वल्गितास्फोटितोत्कृष्टैः पुण्यैर्गन्धैश्च सेवितम् ॥४१॥
verses.english: The dependents of the god were engaged in singing, in playing upon musical instruments, in dancing, in laughing, in frolicking about and stricking and clapping their palms. The place was also made fragrant with perfumes.

verses.sanskrit: स्तूयमानं स्तवैर्दिव्यैर्ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः।  गोप्तारं सर्वभूतानामिष्वासधरमच्युतम् ॥४२॥
verses.english: Arjuna then beheld that protector of all creatures, that undeteriorating wielder of the bow (Pinaka), eulogised with beautiful panegyrics by the sages and the reciters of the Vedas.
verses.bhavadeepa: लास्यं नृत्यम् । बल्गितमितस्ततः प्रचारः । आस्फोटितं भुजाडम्बरः उत्कुष्टमुच्चैः स्वनितम् ॥४१॥

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेवस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा जगाम शिरसा क्षितिम्। पार्थेन सह धर्मात्मा गृणन् ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥४३॥
verses.english: Beholding the god, the pious-souled son of Vasudeva, together with the son of Pritha, saluted him by touching the earth with his head; and he uttered then the eternal verses from the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: लोकदिं विश्वकर्माणमजमीशानमव्ययम्। मनसः परमं योनिं स्वं वायुं ज्योतिषां निधिम् ॥४४॥
स्रष्टारं वारिधाराणां भुवश्च प्रकृतिं पराम्।  देवदानवयक्षाणां मानवानां च साधनम् ॥४५॥
verses.bhavadeepa: लोकानामादिमुपादानम् । विश्वं जगत्कर्म प्राप्यं यस्य । ईशानमप्रतिहतेच्छम् । अव्ययमविकारम् । मनसः परमं प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिकारणम्। योनिमुत्पत्तिस्थानं च । ज्योतिषां तेजसां निधिमधिष्ठानम् ॥४४॥

verses.sanskrit: योगानां च परं धाम दृष्टं ब्रह्मविदां निधिम्। चराचरस्य स्रष्टारं प्रतिहर्तारमेव च ॥४६॥
verses.english: Then Krishna adored with his speech, his mind, his intellect and his acts that origin of the worlds; that creator of the universe; that unborn divinity; that lord paramount; that undeteriorating che; that primary source from which the mind has sprung; that receptacle of the space, the wind and the luminary bodies; that creator of the rain; that primordial essence of the earth; that one worthy of the reverence of the celestials, the Danavas, the Yakshas and the human beings; that one who is the highest Brahma realised by the Yogins; that protector of those versed in the Vedas; that creator and destroyer of the mobile and immobile creatures, that God whose anger is destruction; that supreme soul; that one who is equal to Shakra or the sun.
verses.bhavadeepa: परां मूलभूतां प्रकृतिं प्रधानं साधनं सिद्धेर्निधानम् ॥४५॥

verses.sanskrit: कालकोपं महात्मानं शक्रसूर्यगुणोदयम्।  ववन्दे तं तदा कृष्णो वाङ्मनोबुद्धिकर्मभिः ॥४७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: योगानां योगदर्शिनां परं धाम परमाश्रयम् । दृष्टं साक्षाद्भूतं ब्रह्मतत्त्वं तद्विदां निधिं रहस्यम् ॥४६॥

verses.sanskrit: यं प्रपद्यन्ति विद्वांसः सूक्ष्माध्यात्मपदैषिणः।  तमजं कारणात्मानं जग्मतुः शरणं भवम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: Then Krishna and Arjuna sought the protection of that Bhava who is uncreate the unmanifest cause and whom sages learned in the Vedas worship when they desire to obtain the subtle and spiritual existence.
verses.bhavadeepa: काल इव कोपो यस्य शक्रस्य गुणा ऐश्वर्यादयः सूर्यस्य गुणाः प्रतापादयः । तेषामुदयो यस्मात् ॥४७॥

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनश्चापि तं देवं भूयो भूयोऽप्यवन्दत।  ज्ञात्वा तं सर्वभूतादिं भूतभव्यभवोद्भवम् ॥४९॥
ततस्तावागतौ दृष्ट्वा नरनारायणावुभौ।  सुप्रसन्नमनाः शर्वः प्रोवाच प्रहसन्निव ॥५०॥
verses.english: Then beholding them two, viz., Nara and Narayana come to him, Sharva with a delightful heart said these words, as if smiling the whileस्वागतं वो नरश्रेष्ठावुत्तिष्ठेतां गतक्लमौ।

verses.sanskrit: स्वागतं वो नरश्रेष्ठावुत्तिष्ठेतां गतक्लमौ।  किं च वामीप्सितं वीरौ मनसः क्षिप्रमुच्यताम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: All hail, O you two foremost of men! Arise and let the fatigue of your journey be shaken off. Tell me soon that things your minds earn after, O you heroes!

verses.sanskrit: येन कार्येण संप्राप्तौ युवां तत्साधयामि किम्।  व्रियतामात्मनः श्रेयस्तत् सर्वं प्रददानि वाम् ॥५२॥
ततस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जली।  वासुदेवार्जुनौ सर्वं तुष्टुवाते महामती ॥५३॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of the god, Vasudeva and Arjuna rose up with their palms folded;

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या स्तवेन दिव्येन महात्मानावनिन्दितौ।                 कृष्णार्जुनावूचतुः। नमो भवाय शर्वाय रुद्राय वरदाय च।  पशूनां पतये नित्यमुग्राय च कपर्दिने ॥५५॥
verses.english: Krishna and Arjuna said Salutation to Bhava, to Sharva and to Rudra the giver of all boons; to the lord of all animate beings; to him who is known as Kapardin; to the great Divinity.

verses.sanskrit: महादेवाय भीमाय त्र्यंबकाय च शान्तये।  ईशानाय मखघ्नाय नमोऽस्त्वन्धकघातिने ॥५६॥
verses.english: To Bhima; to the three-eyed god who is identical with peace; to Isha and to him who annihilates all pride engendered by the possession of prosperity. Salutation to the slayer of Andhaka;

verses.sanskrit: कुमारगुरवे तुभ्यं नीलग्रीवाय वेधसे।  पिनाकिने हविष्याय सत्याय विभवे सदा ॥५७॥
verses.english: To the father of the Kumara (Kartikeya); unto him of blue neck and of great intelligence; unto the wielder of the Pinaka bow; unto the !.avisya; unto him who is ever attended with truth and prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: विलोहिताय धूम्राय व्याधायानपराजिते।  नित्यनीलशिखण्डाय शूलिने दिव्यचक्षुषे ॥५८॥
verses.english: To him who is red; who is tawny, who is the hunter in disguise; and who is unvanquished; unto his who possesses blue locks, who wields the trident, who is omniscient; unto him who is the Hotri and the Pitri; unto him of three-eyes, who is disease and whose vital seed is fire itself; unto him who is inconceivable, who is the lord of the goddess Ambika; who receives homage from all creatures; whose emblem is the bull; whose head is shaved and who wears matted locks and who is again a Brahmacharin, unto him who performs ascetic austerities in the waters, who is devote to the study of the Vedas and who is unvanquished. Unto him who is the soul of the universe, its creator and remains pervading it. Salutation unto him worthy of the homage of all creatures and the origin of all creatures; unto the Brahmachakra, the Sharva, the Shankara and Shiva.

verses.sanskrit: होत्रे पोत्रे त्रिनेत्राय व्याधाय वसुरेतसे।  अचिन्त्यायाम्बिकाभर्त्रे सर्वदेवस्तुताय च ॥५९॥
verses.bhavadeepa: व्याधाय मृगहननात् । द्विरुक्तिर्द्विस्तथाकरणात् । अनान्प्राणिनः पराजयतीति अनपराजित्सर्वभूतोत्तमत्वात् । नीलशिखण्डो नीलकेशत्वात् ॥५८॥

verses.sanskrit: वृषध्वजाय मुण्डाय जटिने ब्रह्मचारिणे।  तप्यमानाय सलिले ब्रह्मण्यायाजिताय च ॥६०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: दीक्षितः भावेन हवनशीलत्वात् । वसुरेता अग्नौ रेतःक्षेपणात् ॥५९॥

verses.sanskrit: विश्वात्मने विश्वसृजे विश्वमावृत्य तिष्ठते।  नमो नमस्ते सेव्याय भूतानां प्रभवे सदा ॥६१॥
ब्रह्मवक्त्राय सर्वाय शंकराय शिवाय च।  नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये प्रजानां पतये नमः ॥६२॥
verses.english: Salutations be unto him who is the lord of speech and the master of the created beings; salutation unto the lord of the universe and of the great people.

verses.sanskrit: नमो विश्वस्य पतये महतां पतये नमः।  नमः सहस्रशिरसे सहस्रभुजमृत्यवे ॥६३॥
verses.english: Salutations unto him of thousand heads who possesses a thousand arms and who is Death himself. Salutations unto him of thousand eyes and legs, whose deeds are countless.
verses.bhavadeepa: ब्रह्मवक्त्रो वेदपूर्णमुखत्वात् । सर्वः सर्वस्वरूपत्वात् । शिवो मोक्षहेतुत्वात् । वाचस्पतिर्वाङ्मयप्रवर्तनात् ॥६२॥

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रनेत्रपादाय नमोऽसंख्येयकर्मणे।  नमो हिरण्यवर्णाय हिरण्यकवचाय च।  भक्तानुकम्पिने नित्यं सिध्यतां नो वरः प्रभो ॥६४॥
verses.english: Salutations unto him of the complexion of gold, who is clad in a armour of gold; and unto him who is ever gracious upon his devotees. O lord let our desires be fulfilled.
verses.bhavadeepa: सहस्त्रभुजाय मृत्यवे च मन्यवे इति पाठः ॥६३॥

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवं स्तुत्वा महादेवं वासुदेवः सहार्जुनः। प्रसादयामास भवं तदा ह्यस्त्रोपलब्धये ॥६५॥
